scientific_hypothesis: Adding a third layer to the two-material system (SiO2/TiO2) provides sufficient degrees of freedom to reduce the arithmetic mean reflectance over 450-700 nm below the ~0.019 level achieved by the optimal 2-layer configuration, potentially approaching the soft target of 0.03 with greater margin or exceeding it significantly.
expected_advantages: Broader spectral low-reflectance region compared to 2-layer design.
Lower arithmetic mean reflectance due to extra tuning parameter.
Potential to push mean reflectance well below 0.01.
known_risks: Optimizer may converge to a local minimum where the third layer has negligible effect (thickness near bound or effectively zero optical impact).
Increased complexity might lead to thinner layers approaching the 40 nm lower bound, increasing sensitivity to fabrication errors (though not modeled here).
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should converge to a value corresponding to a mean reflectance significantly lower than a single-layer benchmark, potentially approaching but not guaranteed to reach the 0.03 soft target.

If the hypothesis fails (e.g., due to bandwidth limitations), best_target_score will plateau at a level corresponding to a mean reflectance > 0.03, and tightest_margin may indicate the solution is pushing against thickness bounds.
valid_candidates should remain > 0 throughout the search unless the bounds are mutually exclusive with physical resonance conditions (unlikely here).
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to historical best is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge search as stagnated -> stop and retain current best.
If valid_candidates = 0, judge constraint set infeasible -> relax total thickness budget or review bounds, do not re-run the same route.

If the final mean reflectance > 0.05, conclude that a two-layer system with these specific materials and bounds is insufficient for the target, and recommend stopping or changing material set (if allowed in future rounds).
